title: Signal Linux LV2 And Backend Boundary Demo

launch.notes: Runs the existing Linux LV2 execution and Linux audio-backend boundary descriptor and acceptance lanes, records one machine-readable receipt, and emits a rendered operator companion.

scenarios.title: Linux LV2 And Backend Boundary Bootstrap
scenarios.summary: Captures the existing Linux LV2 broker-backed execution boundary and Linux backend identity boundary through one repo-owned live demo surface.

evidence.notes: This bootstrap surface wraps the existing Linux LV2 execution and Linux audio-backend boundary descriptors plus their current acceptance lanes while adding a rendered operator companion and without inventing a plugin browser or new host UI.

known_exclusions: Plugin capability browsing remains deferred to a later g09.012 planning decision.
This surface is Linux-specific and does not claim macOS AU/CoreAudio breadth or generalized cross-platform plugin browsing.
This demo does not claim live Linux device ownership, distro-wide certification, or UI/editor hosting breadth.
expected_checks: The receipt captures the machine-readable Linux LV2 execution boundary descriptor.
The receipt captures the machine-readable Linux audio-backend boundary descriptor.
The receipt records that the existing Linux LV2 execution and Linux audio-backend acceptance lanes completed successfully.
The rendered companion view makes the Linux LV2 and backend boundaries visually inspectable without reading the raw receipt first.
signal-plugin-lv2 only moves to live demo coverage because this manifest and receipt exist.
